The harbor town woke slowly on winter mornings. Fishing boats left before dawn,
and by the time the bakery opened, the first crates of herring were already
stacked on the pier. Children walked to school along the sea wall, counting
gulls and arguing about whose turn it was to carry the football.

In the afternoon the wind usually turned. Shop owners pulled their awnings in,
and the ferry to the island ran late more often than not. Nobody complained
much; the delay gave people time to talk, and talking was what the town did best.
